note: `in-ns` IS A NAMESPACE FORM. `(in-ns 'a.b)` is how a file loaded into a running runtime declares its namespace; `currentNamespace` stayed "user" for it, so every top-level definition in such a file was stranded on owner `user` with NO `contains` edge and the wrong scope — 484 definitions across 17 files, the whole of clojure's own pretty-printer (cl_format 106, pretty_writer 42, core_deftype 40, pprint_base 36, dispatch 35, core_print 25) plus genclass.clj and the clj-kondo corpus. Invisible for three waves because it is an ABSENCE, not a wrong value: a file whose namespace is unknown still emits a full, plausible symbol table, and every per-class completeness claim was true of it. The second half of the class is that a file may SWITCH namespace part-way: the definition after the second `in-ns` belongs to the namespace in force HERE, not to the one the file opened with, so the namespace is resolved POSITIONALLY. `in-ns` takes a QUOTED symbol (a bare `name` field read gives `'a.b`, with the reader quote still on it) and does NOT reset the alias/refer tables, because it switches namespace without re-running `ns`.
